bull_bear.title: Capital allocation

bull_bear.body: High export dependency on US/Europe; macroeconomic slowdown in key export markets; delayed adoption of AI; potential margin compression if HA Plus scaling fails; regulatory risks from RPTs with Honda Motor Co. Ltd.; currency volatility.
bull_bear.title: Risks & watch-items

bull_bear.body: Confident and defensive; acknowledged revenue decline but emphasized profitability gains and strategic pivot; optimistic on domestic infrastructure demand; proactive on shareholder communication but non-committal on forward guidance; tone suggests prioritization of cash returns and domestic growth over export recovery.
bull_bear.title: Management quality / tone

bull_bear.body: Profit growth despite revenue drop is not just from interest income — it reflects a structural shift from low-margin export sales to high-margin domestic sales, implying a deliberate de-risking of revenue base; the HA Plus initiative may be the first step toward becoming a B2B engine supplier to Indian construction OEMs, not just a product seller.
bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Technology access through the collaboration agreement with Honda Motor Co., Ltd., Japan, dated 18.10.1985, renewed from time to time and valid till March 31, 2027, including on-the-job training and guidance for the Company's engineers and technicians
- Stated leadership position in the portable generator segment in India
- Stated leadership position in the water pump segment, with 2-inch water pump sales crossing 60,000+ units during the financial year
- Honda brand water pumps preferred for unmatched fuel efficiency, reliability and portability
- Fuel-efficient 4-stroke technology delivering significant savings in total cost of operation versus low-cost imported alternatives
- Distribution and demand-creation reach via dedicated demonstration vans and manpower deployment across agriculture and construction segments
- Cost reduction through import substitution, benchmarking, value engineering and localization with the support of HM Japan
- Adoption of Global Honda Standards to increase process efficiency
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Government subsidy scheme delays holding back farm-equipment demand — Subsidy policies of state and central governments and the associated complex disbursement processes delay timely delivery of goods to end customers; FY 2025-26 was challenging for the tiller market as customers deferred purchases in anticipation of scheme releases that were subsequently delayed.
- Low-cost imports, primarily from China, disrupting brush-cutter pricing — The influx of low-cost imported brush cutters has disrupted market pricing, forcing the Company to defend on total cost of operation and quality messaging rather than price.
- US import tariff volatility and tightening overseas product regulation — Frequent changes in USA import tariffs have impacted certainty and price competitiveness, potentially influencing demand and order inflows, while stricter CARB/EPA/CPSC regulations are impacting prospective sales — a direct exposure given exports contribute 22% of total turnover.
- Evolving global environmental regulation raising compliance cost — BRSR flags a continuing challenge from the dynamic and evolving landscape of global environmental regulations, where compliance requires substantial investment in infrastructure, continuous updates on legal frameworks and awareness-building among process stakeholders.
- Structural erosion of urban backup-power demand — Peak power deficit continues to be within acceptable levels due to adequate power generation, so interim demand in urban areas driven by long-haul power cuts has been on a reducing trend — eroding the traditional core driver of generator sales.
- Weak consumer spending and discretionary demand — Consumer spending remains low due to higher interest rates, and corporate/institutional demand remained subdued during the year due to deferment of funds.
- Competition from global players with optimized supply chains and aggressive pricing — A key challenge especially in new and emerging export markets where price sensitivity is high.
- Dependence on Honda Motor Co., Ltd., Japan for manufacturing process and technology — BRSR identifies the process as evolved with technical inputs and support from Honda Motor Co., Ltd., Japan under a technical collaboration agreement — a significant entry barrier for new entrants, but also a structural dependency the Company's access to best-available processes rests on.
- Natural resource use and waste management in manufacturing — BRSR flags society-related risk from use of natural resources such as water and air in the manufacturing process, mitigated through infrastructure to minimize resource consumption and full compliance with waste-management regulation.
- Cyber and information-security risk from an evolving digital risk landscape — Increasing cyber threats and regulatory expectations require ongoing investment in data security, operational resilience and business continuity, addressed via strengthened policies, advanced monitoring and threat detection, and regular vulnerability assessments and risk audits.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

business.body: The Company manufactures and sells portable gensets, general-purpose GX engines, water pumps (1.5 inch to 4 inch outlet sizes), 4-stroke brush cutters, power tillers and allied engine-driven equipment such as crop harvesters, backpack sprayers, concrete cutters and plate compactors. Domestic customers span farmers, small and medium businesses, construction users, and corporate/institutional buyers across urban, semi-urban and rural India, supported by promotional and demonstration activity including dedicated demonstration vans. Exports cover markets including Canada, USA, Australia, Japan, Europe, Indonesia, the Asia Oceania region and Africa, with product specifications upgraded to meet advanced-country regulations.

business.body:
- **Generators:** Portable generators / gensets, 2~3 kVA generator models (export)
- **General purpose engines and water pumping sets:** Honda GX portable engines, Water pumps with 1.5 inch to 4 inch outlet sizes, 2-inch water pumps, Honda GX powered long tail boat application
- **Construction equipment:** Concrete cutters, Plate compactors
- **Agriculture equipment:** Backpack sprayer, Crop harvester
- **Brush cutters:** 4-stroke brush cutters — fixed shaft, flexible shaft and high-powered variants
- **Tillers:** Power tillers

outlook.body:
- Sustain leadership in the portable generator category by tapping new applications (mobile utility vans, doorstep services, drone charging) alongside traditional backup-power demand
- Deepen penetration through promotional efforts focused on urban, semi-urban and rural markets aimed at evolving lifestyle and comfort needs
- Expand the footprint in the construction segment by introducing more engine-driven applications, building on success in global markets
- Develop a multi-channel structure across segments to expand the application-oriented product and equipment portfolio
- Build a robust ecosystem through partnerships with small, medium and specialized players as well as OEMs to enhance cost competitiveness and strengthen application-specific product sales and services
- Drive farm mechanization with engines, water pumps, brush cutters, power tillers and crop harvesters as farm labour declines
- Expand demonstration activities with dedicated demonstration vans and manpower for newly launched agriculture and construction products
- Counter low-cost Chinese brush-cutter imports by communicating the total-cost-of-operation advantage of 4-stroke technology and product quality through proactive marketing campaigns in key focus markets
- Strengthen engagement with channel partners in export markets to expand reach and drive demand for gasoline-fuelled tillers, engines and water pumps
- Engage closely with government stakeholders through field teams to speed up implementation of subsidy schemes for farm equipment
- Strengthen human capital through capability building, leadership development, succession planning and a diverse, equitable and inclusive workplace
- Accelerate Green HRM through increased digitalization of HR processes and reduced paper usage
- Strengthen IT governance and cybersecurity posture through information security policies and controls, advanced monitoring and threat detection, and regular vulnerability assessments and risk audits
- The Company follows a formal Dividend Distribution Policy adopted pursuant to Regulation 43A of the SEBI Listing Regulations and published on its website. Distribution during the year under review was made through two interim dividends declared by the Board — Rs. 100/- per equity share of Rs. 10/- each (1000% of face value) on August 12, 2025 and Rs. 3.50/- per equity share (35% of face value) on February 13, 2026 — with the Directors recommending a further final dividend of Rs. 23/- per equity share (230% of face value) based on the Company's performance for the year ended March 31, 2026, subject to Members' approval at the ensuing Annual General Meeting. There was no change in the share capital of the Company during the year, indicating no equity issuance or buyback activity. Governance of capital and financial matters is supported by a Board Committee on Financial Matters alongside the Audit Committee, which oversees the financial reporting process, internal financial controls, risk management and related-party transactions. Independent Directors are paid only sitting fees (Rs. 1,00,000 per Board meeting, Rs. 60,000 per Audit Committee meeting and Rs. 50,000 per other Committee meeting) and no commission on net profit is paid to any Director.
- Carbon emission reduction targets set with defined timelines: 74.75 tons for 2025-26 and 120.14 tons for 2026-27
- During 2025-26 the Company achieved a CO2 reduction of 74.75 tons against a target of 42.74 tons
- The Board's Report commits to a further 2.5% reduction in CO2 emissions during the financial year 2026-27, supported by a dedicated Safety & Environmental team, with practices extended across key suppliers and service providers
- ISO 9001 certified; also certified/compliant to IS 7347 for Engines, IS 11501 for Water Pump, CPCB-IV+ Indian Emission Standard for Portable Genset, EU REACH (EC No 1907/2006), EU RoHS (Directive 2011/65/EU), EPA & CARB 40 CFR for US 7kVA Genset, CSA CoC C22.2 #100 for Canada 7kVA Genset, Europe Sample Fit Test 97/68/EC and Europe Noise Directive 2000/14/EC for EU 7kVA Genset, and CPCB Plastic Waste and Battery Waste Management Rules
- Health, Safety and Environment (HSE) Policy with an HSE management system on a 'Plan-Do-Check-Act' methodology, covering risk assessments for workplace safety, fire hazards, process safety, chemical safety, machinery-related risks and occupational health, with regular audits
- Board-approved policies covering all nine NGRBC principles, translated into procedures and extended to value chain partners for eight of the nine principles
- Guiding principle of being 'a Company that society wants to exist', driving production and sale of environment-friendly products that meet all regulatory standards, with strict waste management protocols
- Energy conservation programme delivering measured savings — including IGBT switching in the varnish machine at the alternator shop, an energy-efficient mist collector on grinding machines, dust-collector and blower-motor frequency optimization, LED replacement on assembly lines, and thermal painting on PDC furnaces reducing PNG gas consumption
- Diversity: women represent 12.5% of the Board of Directors and 25% of Key Management Personnel; focused initiatives to enhance gender diversity and equitable access to opportunities
- Green HRM initiatives accelerated through increased digitalization of HR processes and minimized paper usage
- CSR interventions in education, community development and environmental sustainability, with a stated commitment to measurable and sustainable social impact
- Grievance redressal mechanisms in place for shareholders, employees and workers, customers and value chain partners, with no complaints filed under any NGRBC principle in FY 2025-26 or the previous year
- BRSR reported on a standalone basis with no reasonable assurance obtained on the BRSR core
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The routed sections disclose no named plant, capacity or capex project with a commissioning timeline. Expansion is described as portfolio-, application- and channel-led rather than capacity-led: the Company is actively working to expand its footprint in the construction segment by introducing more engine-driven applications, having launched concrete cutters and plate compactors for the construction industry in the previous financial year, and has introduced a backpack sprayer for plant-protection spraying and equipment washing plus a crop harvester for quick harvesting of crops. It expanded reach into coastal areas and waterways with a Honda GX powered long tail boat application for small and medium sized boats in inland waterways and offshore fishing, and continued to expand its range of power tillers to support agricultural mechanization. Distribution-side expansion is being pursued through a multi-channel structure across segments and partnerships with small, medium and specialized players as well as OEMs, backed by dedicated demonstration vans and manpower deployment for recently launched agriculture and construction products. On the environment side, the Company has committed to a further 2.5% reduction in CO2 emissions during the financial year 2026-27, supported by a dedicated Safety & Environmental team.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Weather-related power outages continue to drive demand for generators as backup power sources
- Portable generators increasingly used for primary applications — mobile utility vans, mobile salons, pet grooming, food trucks — and for charging drones used in agriculture and defence
- Demand for portable generators from milking, chilling and leisure uses such as camping is expected to remain strong
- Generator sales for backup power in small hotels and homestays in Jammu & Kashmir were adversely affected after the Pahalgam attacks led to a sharp decline in tourist inflow
- Corporate and institutional demand remained subdued during the year due to deferment of funds but is expected to recover in this fiscal
- Economic activity among small and medium sized businesses is picking up, with demand for portable backup power expected to grow steadily
- Peak power deficit remains within acceptable levels on adequate generation, so interim urban demand driven by long-haul power cuts is on a reducing trend
- Consumer spending remains low due to higher interest rates
- Unseasonal and uneven monsoon distribution lifted water pump sales in FY 2025-26 across eastern, central and southern markets
- Delays in state and central government support programmes for farming and fisheries, and in the release of government funds, held back demand and deferred customer purchases, notably in tillers
- Construction mechanization for small, portable and compact machines saw healthy growth on continued infrastructure development focus
- Government's planned investments in irrigation and infrastructure are expected to drive demand for fuel-based engines; infrastructure momentum expected from national highways, warehousing, airports and urban/rural housing
- Growing environmental awareness is driving demand for more fuel-efficient 4-stroke engine powered applications
- Export business outperformed plan, led by 2~3 kVA generator models in Canada, USA, Australia, Japan, Europe and Indonesia; water pump and tiller sales showing increasing acceptability in the Asia Oceania region
- Frequent changes in USA import tariffs have impacted certainty and price competitiveness, potentially influencing demand and order inflows
- Stricter CARB/EPA/CPSC regulations are impacting prospective export sales
- Low-cost imported brush cutters, primarily from China, have disrupted market pricing
- Margin pressure attributed by management to higher material cost and an exceptional item relating to the new direct wage code
outlook.title: Demand & outlook drivers

deepdive.thesis: Honda India Power Products delivered a profit-before-tax increase despite revenue decline in FY24 due to strong domestic sales and higher other income, signaling resilience in local markets; strategic shift toward HA Plus construction segment and reduced export reliance positions it for margin expansion in FY25-26, though export headwinds remain a near-term constraint.

open.item: The Company plans to achieve a further 2.5% reduction in CO2 emissions during the financial year 2026-27.
The imported-technology collaboration agreement with Honda dated 18.10.1985, renewed/revamped from time to time, is valid for a period of 5 years till March 31, 2027 — a renewal milestone to track.
Corporate and institutional demand, subdued this year due to deferment of funds, is expected to recover in this fiscal.
Implementation of a 300 KW capacity Solar Power Plant, whose feasibility study was completed in 2023-2024, will start in FY 2029-2030.
Adoption of the global concept for domestic Engines and Gensets with E10, with a subsequent rollout plan for E20 gasoline.
Developing a new electrified power unit for Japan, US, EU and other advanced nations, and adopting electrified power unit technology into operations.

Further absorption of imported technology for localization of high-technology engine components and country-specific models, including OHV engine value engineering, generator fuel-injection/inverter/GCU technology, Bluetooth and CO-sensor enabled products, and high-performance self-priming pumps for Indian farmers.
The Company is actively working to expand its footprint in the construction segment by introducing more engine-driven applications, building on its success in global markets.

The Company is focused on developing a multi-channel structure across various segments to expand its application-oriented product and equipment portfolio, with partnerships with small, medium and specialized players and OEMs expected to enhance cost competitiveness.
The Company will continue to strengthen engagement with channel partners to expand reach and drive demand for gasoline-fuelled tillers, engines and water pumps.

The Company will focus on communicating the total-cost-of-operation advantage of its 4-stroke brush cutter technology and product quality through proactive marketing campaigns in key focus markets to help stabilize market pricing.
Frequent changes in USA import tariffs have impacted certainty and price competitiveness, potentially influencing demand and order inflows.
Stricter CARB/EPA/CPSC regulations are impacting prospective export sales.
Subsidy policies of state and central governments and associated operational processes delay delivery of goods and defer end-customer purchases, particularly in tillers and brush cutters.
Peak power deficit remaining within acceptable levels means interim urban demand driven by long-haul power cuts is on a reducing trend.
Competition from global players with optimized supply chains, logistics routes and aggressive pricing remains a key challenge, especially in new and emerging price-sensitive markets.
